content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Tacoma

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of education and project management experience. Review PMI's specific requirements for your background—whether you hold a bachelor's degree, associate degree, or high school diploma determines your minimum hours of direct project experience. Gather documentation of your experience before applying.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. Attend all sessions synchronously from anywhere, interact with active certified practitioners, and cover the full PMBOK® Guide framework. This formal education satisfies PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement and prepares you for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Create your PMI account and submit your official PMP application directly to the Project Management Institute. You'll provide proof of your education, project experience, and completion of the 35 contact-hour course. Pay PMI's exam fee to finalize your eligibility and receive authorization to sit for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor support—to reinforce course content. Schedule your exam at a testing center or online proctored location. On exam day, demonstrate your mastery of project management processes and earn your PMP credential.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: The PMP credential is valid for three years. During your renewal cycle, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, conference attendance, volunteer work, or publishing. Submit your PDU record to PMI before expiration to keep your certification active and demonstrate ongoing professional commitment.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.
